summary: The options both entry points accept. One table, so a POSIX shell and PowerShell cannot drift.
why: Two hand-written argument parsers in two languages are two contracts that agree until the day they do not.
This file is the one they are both checked against: auto-pigeon-tools/tests/test_aucom_native.py fails when either script accepts an option this table does not name, or omits one it does.

options.name: --out
options.summary: where the result bundle is written (default: acceptance-bundle beside the Companion)

options.name: --tool-path
options.summary: the ROOT of an EricW build you already have; the profile finds bin/qbsp under it

options.name: --engine
options.summary: an engine executable you already have; needs --game-root too

options.name: --game-root
options.summary: a game installation you already own; no byte of it is copied, hashed or uploaded

options.name: --only
options.summary: run only these lanes, comma separated

options.name: --skip
options.summary: run everything but these lanes, comma separated

options.name: --companion
options.summary: the Companion to run; the default is the one beside this script

options.name: --no-checksums
options.summary: skip the checksum verification and record that it was skipped, rather than claiming it passed

always_reported: --entry-point  which of the two scripts ran
--shell        what that script is running under
--host-arch    what the operating system calls this machine, so an emulated artifact is not reported as native
--checksums    pass, fail or not_available — the SHELL's answer, because a program cannot vouch for its own bytes
